hypothesis: The one train failure (mqx-071) came from a reasoning mistake that could recur, not from missing knowledge. The neuro exam came back with an abnormal objective finding (bilateral decreased hearing). The patient said his hearing hadn't changed, and the doctor trusted that over the exam. It never ordered audiometry to settle the conflict. It then submitted a closely related diagnosis that leaves that finding unexplained (vestibular neuritis instead of labyrinthitis), even though its own notes flagged the gap. It also used 2 of its 5 requests re-asking for exam details the record had already said were unavailable. These cases are vignettes, so abnormal findings are planted on purpose to separate neighbouring diagnoses. A required pre-submit check should catch this on unseen cases in any specialty: list every abnormal finding, make sure the diagnosis explains all of them, trust objective findings over the patient's impression and confirm with the matching test, and pick explicitly between near-identical diagnoses. Caveat: this rests on a single failure (19/20 on train). The earlier dev score of 0.775 suggests held-out cases fail for other reasons this batch doesn't show.
changes: harness/system.md: added a short step-by-step workflow (history → exams/tests that tell the leading diagnoses apart → stop re-requesting anything marked 'not in the record') and a required 'Findings check' before submit_diagnosis. The check says: every abnormal finding is a clue and the diagnosis must explain all of them; objective findings outrank the patient's self-report and should be confirmed by the matching test; decide explicitly which feature separates two close diagnoses; submit the most specific diagnosis, not a broad category.

harness/lessons.md: added two general lessons. Don't explain away an objective deficit the patient denies; confirm it with a test and let it decide between neighbouring diagnoses. Don't re-request details the record says are unavailable.
expected_effect: Fewer 'neighbouring variant' errors, where the doctor picks the sibling diagnosis that misses one planted abnormal finding (e.g. labyrinthitis vs neuritis, or acute vs chronic forms of a disease). It should also order more confirmatory tests when exam and history disagree, and waste fewer requests. I expect a small accuracy gain on held-out cases and little risk of regression, since the workflow mostly sets out what the doctor already does on the cases it gets right.
